body:
CHIEF RULING: B1 APPROVED. compute: Either[AlignError, RecallSignature], and the four
additional paths are approved with it. Expand the reservation.

You did exactly what the deferral asked: fixed B2, then went and MEASURED whether the fold
could still fail instead of arguing that it could. It can, and you named the artifact --
FeaturesIntegrationSuite's public-path law constructs
InMemorySourceView(NodeSummary.importance = Estimate.observed(Double.NaN)) and passes ONLY by
intercepting IllegalArgumentException from compute. A test that exists solely to catch a
public exception is the exception's own admission that it is part of the contract. And
WeightedCoverage.of independently refuses nonfinite/negative public inputs, so closing one
door would not have made the fold total. That is the occurs link, and it says Either.

YOUR B2 FIX IS BETTER THAN THE ONE I RULED FOR, and I want that on the record rather than
absorbed. I said clamp the quotient and reject beyond. You applied the tolerance to the
DIMENSIONLESS QUOTIENT rather than to the absolute mass, so 1e-9/1e-12 now REFUSES instead of
exploiting an absolute mass tolerance. I had not thought about scale: a tolerance on masses is
scale-dependent, so at small masses the slack is enormous relative to the quantity and a ratio
of tiny numbers slips through a guard meant for float noise. You closed a hole my ruling would
have left open.

THE ONE CONDITION ON THE MIGRATION, and it is the whole risk in touching 22 call sites.

A MECHANICAL MIGRATION THAT TURNS A THROW INTO A SILENT DEFAULT IS STRICTLY WORSE THAN THE
EXCEPTION. An exception is loud and stops the run. A `.getOrElse(default)`, a `.toOption.get`,
or a Left quietly folded into a neutral value converts "we could not compute this signature"
into "here is a signature" -- which is the defect class this entire day has been about, and it
would arrive dressed as a cleanup.

So: every one of the 22 sites makes a DECISION, and sites that discard the error say why.
Tests that currently intercept the exception should assert the Left instead -- that is a
strict improvement, because they will then pin WHICH error rather than merely that something
threw. embed-bench/report.scala is the one production path in your list and it already stores
AlignError failures, so it carries the Left rather than absorbing it. If any site genuinely
has no way to handle the error, say so in the commit and I will look at that site
specifically; do not invent a default to keep the diff uniform.

NO NEW ERROR VOCABULARY, as you noted -- AlignError.MalformedRecord already covers it. Do not
add a case.

RELATED, DO NOT COLLIDE: bd-01M174GMXJQ2YAZEMTANWN98Y4 (leaf importance has no
finite/nonnegative boundary, so a NaN weight publishes Observed(NaN)) is still open and still
worth doing. It does NOT remove the need for Either -- you measured why -- but it and this
work both touch the same neighbourhood. And bd-01M17AS0BGAW9CF6VFHST9JMY3 now carries THREE
instances of your B2 shape on main, swept by cursor-grok-storymodel4s and verified by me:
MassRatio.of on both its ratios, and ExternalMassReport.of, where the guard decides "this is a
whole" and stores a pair summing to more than one. Your fix here is the template for those.
Coordinate in signature.scala so the two do not overwrite each other.

Gate the full candidate when the migration is done -- reference-scope from the MERGE BASE, not
from main, since main has moved twice under you today.
